name: Sombre Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Halmahera (northern moluccas)
description: A large forest kingfisher with a dark back, white underparts, and a white eyebrow and collar. Back color is earth-brown in females and tinged with green in males.

name: Gray-legged Tinamou
rangeDescription: Tropical forest of east-central colombia to southern venezuela
description: Unobtrusive, poorly-known tinamou. Mostly rusty-colored with a scaly back and wings.

name: Vanikoro Monarch
rangeDescription: Vanikoro (southeastern temotu, southeastern solomon islands)
description: A rather chunky flycatcher, mostly dark slate-gray with a pale eye-ring and obvious white undertail. Sometimes cocks and slightly fans tail, especially if aggravated.

name: Red-shouldered Tanager
rangeDescription: The guianas and southern venezuela to northeastern peru and amazonian brazil
description: Locally-distributed, easily-overlooked tanager. Often in pairs; male is almost entirely black with obscure red-and-white patch at base of wing, most visible in flight; female is gray and brown.

name: Seram Boobook
rangeDescription: Seram island (southern moluccas)
description: Large dark-eyed boobook, endemic to Seram, where it inhabits lowland and foothill forests. Very different from other boobooks, with its finely barred white belly and dark brown eyes.

name: Sangihe Whistler
rangeDescription: Sangihe islands (north of sulawesi)
description: A chunky, dingy-looking, thick-billed songbird. Upperparts dark olive-brown, with a grayish head and a pale buff wash on the underparts.

name: Przevalski's Pinktail
rangeDescription: Mountains of western china and eastern tibet
description: The Przevalksi’s Pinktail is the only member of its family. It looks like a cross between a rosefinch and a bunting, but it isn’t closely related to either.

name: Gray-chested Babbler
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria to southern cameroon, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and western kenya; bioko
description: Unusual thrush-like bird with bright reddish-brown upperparts and gray underparts. Found in the understory of montane forest, often in thick and moist areas.

name: Norfolk Island Gerygone
rangeDescription: Norfolk island
description: Nondescript little gray-brown bird with whitish underparts, a thin black bill, and a slender dark line going through the eye. Also note faint white crescents sometimes visible above and below each eye.

name: Buffy-fronted Seedeater
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Large finchlike bird with a strong bill with obviously curved mandibles. Males have a distinctive face pattern—a gray head with a broken pale eyebrow, and a prominent pale mustache and throat.

name: South Moluccan Cicadabird
rangeDescription: Southern moluccas (ambon and seram)
description: Small cuckooshrike with a restricted range, found only on the South Moluccan islands. Males are grayish.

name: Gilt-edged Tanager
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern bahia and southeastern minas gerais to eastern são paulo)
description: Small and brightly colored tanager found in the canopy and subcanopy of montane forests and second growth. Usually in pairs or small groups and often accompanies mixed-species flocks.

name: Gray-backed Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern siberia, manchuria, and northern korea; winters to southeastern asia
description: Brightly colored thrush of well-shaded undergrowth in a variety of habitats, from deep hilly forests to city parks and gardens. Male has clean pale gray upperparts and a bright orange belly, female and immature male replace gray with brown and have dark streaking on the throat and chest.

name: Snethlage's Antpitta
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil (south of the amazon river and east of the xingu, eastward to western maranhão)
description: Plump, almost tailless, cryptically-plumaged bird with an orange eyering. Has a gray crown, an olive-green back, and white underparts with rusty flanks and a black-streaked breast.

name: Patagonian Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Open plains of southern chile and southern argentina
description: Fairly common to uncommon, but often rather local in Patagonian steppe and grassland, often with nearby stony areas and low banks or bluffs. Found in pairs or flocks, and like other yellow-finches feeds mainly on the ground.

name: Half-collared Sparrow
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro to rio grande do sul)
description: Boldly-patterned sparrow found in the understory of humid forest and second growth; usually difficult to see. Note the bicolored bill (black above and bright yellow below) and black patches on either side of the breast.

name: Maquis Canastero
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Slender and long-tailed canastero of the high Andes from Cochabamba, Bolivia south to NE Argentina. Prefers scrubby hillsides, ravines, and open Polylepis woodland above treeline.

name: Short-clawed Lark
rangeDescription: Southeastern botswana and north-central south africa
description: A long, slim pipit-like lark with a slender bill, a bold white eyebrow, and warm-and-dark spangled upperparts. Pairs forage for invertebrates in open thorny savanna, preferring short-cropped grass and open grazed fields.

name: Pin-tailed Snipe
rangeDescription: Siberia; winters india to southeastern asia, indonesia, and philippines
description: Cryptic shorebird of wetlands, wet meadows, and both flooded and dry agricultural fields. Extremely similar in appearance to other snipe, particularly Swinhoe's Snipe; careful study and photography usually required to confirm identification.

name: White-faced Cuckoo-Dove
rangeDescription: Sulawesi and the togian islands
description: A large, unmistakable long-tailed dove with an all-dark body and a contrasting cream-colored face. Also displays a red eye-ring and an iridescent emerald green shawl on the nape.
